evidence: app/package.json:9-12 — astro 7.4.4 / @astrojs/node 11.1.9, the current stable pair as of 2026-10-28
app/astro.config.mjs:4-8 — output: 'server' + node({mode:'standalone'}), matches the current docs' SSR recipe
app/src/pages/404.astro:3 and app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:34 — Astro.response.status, still documented in the astro@7 render-context types
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:15 and app/src/pages/index.astro:7 — Astro.params / Astro.url.searchParams, current APIs
app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:1 — raw process.env.API_BASE_URL where astro:env's schema (envField) is the current typed recommendation
latest_apis.rationale: Everything used is current-generation Astro 7 with no deprecated or removed APIs (checked against the v7 upgrade guide and astro@7 context types); the only miss is not adopting the astro:env schema or typed Props interfaces where they now exist.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:44-52 — global fetch with promise-based in-memory caching instead of a client library
app/src/pages/index.astro:101-103 — FormData + URLSearchParams to read native form state
app/src/pages/index.astro:116-118 — DOMParser for partial HTML swapping, keeping the app framework-free
app/src/styles/global.css:1-30 — design tokens as CSS custom properties, plain CSS, system font stack
app/src/pages/index.astro:97-115 — race protection is a hand-rolled requestId counter; the stale fetch is never aborted (no AbortController)
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:234 — computed inline width for stat bars rather than a CSS custom property
platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first (fetch, FormData, DOMParser, custom properties, native form controls) and adds no JS framework; only small gaps — no AbortController for the search requests and inline styles where a custom property would be more flexible.

evidence: app/package.json:9-12 — exactly two runtime deps: astro and @astrojs/node, both at the latest stable versions
app/package.json:5-7 — scripts are plain astro build / node ./dist/server/entry.mjs, no bundler wrappers or extra tooling
app/src — no client framework, no CSS framework, no lodash-style utilities (mapLimit and debounce are ~20 hand-written lines in lib/pokeapi.ts:91-108)
dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: the framework, its official Node adapter, and nothing else; every hand-rolled helper (concurrency limiter, debounce, cache) is small and lives in one place where the platform offered no direct primitive.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:41 — getJson returns Promise<any>: the app's most volatile boundary (PokeAPI payloads) is untyped across every page
app/tsconfig.json:6 — strict:false deliberately disables the strictness astro/tsconfigs/base sets by default
app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:23-26, abilities/[name].astro:20-23, types/[name].astro:14-17, pokemon/[name].astro:31-34 — the same NotFoundError try/catch + 404 block copy-pasted into four pages
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:51-158 — ~110 lines of move-table business logic (method ordering, enrichment) embedded in the page frontmatter rather than the lib layer
app/src/pages/index.astro:120 — manual history.pushState with no popstate listener: back/forward desyncs URL and results, and this code is outside any framework abstraction that would fix it for you
app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:1-7 and app/src/lib/data.ts:24-36 — API base URL, caching and every index build centralized behind two modules (good)
app/src/styles/global.css — 772-line global stylesheet; components like PokemonCard.astro carry no scoped styles, so markup changes require editing a distant file
churn_resistance.rationale: The data layer is well-isolated, so an API or adapter change touches few files — but types are abandoned at the boundary, the not-found flow is duplicated four times, and one page owns a large block of business logic; a requirements change to moves or 404 handling ripples across pages.

findings.issue: Client-side navigation pushes history entries but there is no popstate listener, so browser back/forward changes the URL while leaving stale results on screen.
findings.suggestion: Add a popstate handler that re-fetches the results for the new URL (or reuse the same fetch path), or adopt Astro's ClientRouter so navigation lifecycle is framework-owned.

findings.issue: strict:false overrides the strict defaults from astro/tsconfigs/base, disabling the framework's intended safety net and making future Astro type changes invisible until runtime.
findings.suggestion: Drop the strict override and enable strict mode; type the few newly-tricky spots with explicit annotations.

findings.issue: getJson(): Promise<any> — every PokeAPI payload (species, pokemon, moves, types) flows through the app untyped, so API shape changes surface as runtime breakage.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces (or at minimum the consumed fields) for the entities in lib and have getJson return a generic, e.g. getJson<T>(path): Promise<T>, with types at the pages' boundaries.

findings.issue: The NotFoundError try/catch + Astro.response.status = 404 pattern is duplicated in four route files; Astro 7.4 also ships a notFound() handler concept for centralized 404 flows.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared loader helper (e.g. loadOr404(() => getJson(...))) into lib, so the not-found policy lives in one place.

findings.issue: API_BASE_URL is read from raw process.env, which the Node adapter permits but is not the current typed recommendation (astro:env with envField validates and types it).
findings.suggestion: Declare API_BASE_URL in env.schema via envField.string({ context: 'server', access: 'public', default: ... }) and import from astro:env/server.

findings.issue: Search races are guarded by a requestId counter; stale fetches still download and parse, wasting bandwidth on every keystroke.
findings.suggestion: Keep an AbortController per request and abort the previous one when a new navigation starts.

findings.issue: npm start runs node ./dist/server/entry.mjs directly; when PORT is unset the Node adapter standalone entry defaults to 8080 (per @astrojs/node source), while the spec's default is 3000.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the start script (e.g. node -e or a small server script) that falls back to 3000, or set the adapter's port option to 3000.

findings.issue: Move-table assembly (version-group fetching, enrichment, method ordering with a hardcoded priority map) lives in the page frontmatter, so it cannot be reused and is the largest single block of logic in the app.
findings.suggestion: Move move-grouping and enrichment into src/lib (e.g. getMovesForGame(pokemon, groupName)) and keep the page a thin consumer.

findings.issue: All component styling (772 lines) is centralized in one global sheet instead of Astro's scoped component styles, coupling component markup to a distant file.
findings.suggestion: Move component-specific rules (pokemon-card, type-badge, evolution tree) into scoped <style> blocks in the .astro components; keep only tokens and layout primitives global.

summary: This is a current-generation Astro 7.4 app with a textbook-lean dependency set (framework + official Node adapter only) and a well-centralized data layer, so framework or API upgrades would touch very few files. It loses forward-thinking points on typing — strict mode is deliberately disabled and every API payload crosses the boundary as any — plus a four-times-duplicated 404 handler and a hand-rolled history navigation with no popstate handling that will need fixing by the next owner. Overall a solid, modern base that mainly needs types and a couple of extracted helpers to age gracefully.

apis.replacement: astro:env schema (envField.string) with astro:env/server import — the current typed recommendation; process.env remains supported for the Node adapter
